sources.title: Alternative Computing Technologies Lab
sources.text: ACT Lab Alternative Computing Technologies ( ACT ) Lab School of Computer Science Georgia Institute of Technology Welcome to Alternative Computing Technologies (ACT) Lab. The ACT Lab is founded by Hadi Esmailzadeh , the Catherine M. and James E. Allchin Early Career Professor of Computer Science at Georgia Institute of Technology. We are working on developing new technologies and cross-stack solutions to improve the performance and energy efficiency of computer systems for emerging applications. News Hadi has won the Air Force Young Investigator Award in 2017. Hadi has won the Microsoft Research Award in 2016. Hadi has won the Lockheed Inspirational Young Faculty Award in 2016. Hadi has won the Qualcomm Research Award in 2016. Tabla's source code has been released and made open source. Our Tabla paper presented in March 2016 at the IEEE Symposium on High Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA '16) has won the distinguished paper award. Chenkai has won the Georgia Tech President's Undergraduate Research Award (PURA) in 2016. Divya has been selected as a finalist of Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship in 2016. Hadi has won the Google Faculty Research Award in 2016. Amir has won the Microsoft Research Fellowship in 2016. Joon has won the Georgia Tech President's Undergraduate Research Award (PURA) in 2015. The Analog Acceleration paper has been selected for honorable mention in IEEE Micro Top Picks from the 2014 Computer Architecture Conferences. The Analog Acceleration paper presented in June 2014 at the International Symposium on Computer Architecture was nominated for consideration for CACM Research highlight. The Data Center Acceleration paper presented in June 2014 at the International Symposium on Computer Architecture was nominated for consideration for CACM Research highlight. Our team, Amir Yazdanbakhsh (CS) and Bradley Thwaites (ECE), has won the Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship . Only 9 teams out of 137 submissions have been selected to receive the fellowship based on their proposals and their presentations. We represent Georgia Institute of Technology. Hadi has won the Google Faculty Research Award in 2014. Our team Amir Yazdanbakhsh and Bradley Thwaites are finalists for Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship . Hadi did an interview with Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) on dark silicon and approximate computing . The NPU paper presented in December 2012 at the International Symposium on Microarchitecture (MICRO '12) is selected for CACM Research Highlights . Sponsors
